_comment: Four probes that between them exercise every oracle kind. Paths are
resolved relative to THIS file. Run with --dry-run first; a dry run
enforces every interlock and stages nothing.
Arm 2 and arm 3 are a matched pair: one payload the engine should accept
and one it should choke on. Keep the poison arm. An arm that should die
and does is what separates 'the engine consumed these bytes' from 'the
engine ignored them', and the container experiment on 2026-08-02 only
concluded anything because it had one.

probes.name: console-smoke
probes.note: Reproduces the 2026-08-02 console proof. Three independent confirmations in one run: MemStats writes a named file, DumpMem writes dump1.mem beside the engine's own control dump0.mem, and Quit ends the process unattended.

probes.name: framelength-half-rate
probes.note: g_framelength ships at 0.05 s = 20 Hz and is runtime-settable. Set it during load and confirm the level still loads and quits cleanly. Bind rather than a bare Win: con_win and con_map are guarded by game state [0x008a9ac0] <= 3 and autoexec.con runs DURING load, so the state at that moment is not yet measured.

probes.name: authored-archive-accept
probes.note: The ACCEPT arm. A same-length authored archive should load and the engine should still be alive at the deadline with no fault log. Fill in the real payload path and its sha256 before running; expectSha256 is not optional, because a probe that stages whatever happens to be at that path measures a different experiment than the one it claims.

probes.name: authored-archive-poison
probes.note: The POISON CONTROL for the arm above, and it must be run every time that arm is run. One invalid opcode killed the engine at about 13 s with 0xC0000005, twice, on 2026-08-02 - which is what proves the engine actually consumes these bytes. If this arm ever stops dying, the accept arm's PASS means nothing.
